brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut and 15-day earlier payment — they keep 7.4% profit vs 5.0% peer, we're tiny (0.01% share) so must bundle volume or play alternates

priceAsk.summary: Ask for ₹0.65–0.80 per piece on caps, a 10–15% reduction
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc (market typical is ₹0.85–0.95/pc; market floor shows headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume)
priceAsk.basis: The market asking price for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, verdict: MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec. They keep 7.4% profit vs 5.0% for similar firms — there's room in their price.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 Days After Receipt to 15 Days After Receipt in exchange for part of the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹1.64 L cash freed up for us if we shorten by 15 days

brief.financialLeverage: PGP is healthy — CARE A+ / Stable rating, ₹3373.51 Cr revenue, keeps 7.4% of every ₹100 sold (peers keep 5.0%) — so they can afford to negotiate. Their cash is tied up for 78 days vs 71 for peers, and they pay suppliers in 29 days vs peer 42 — tighter than most. They borrow at about 7.02%, so paying them 15 days faster is worth roughly that rate to them; trade it for a matching price cut. But we're 0.01% of their sales — tiny — so we must bundle more volume, commit longer, or show them two credible alternates to gain leverage.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B (65/100) — top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma); ₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B (73/100) — robust alternate for bottles/closures

risks: We're only 0.01% of their sales — on our own we have little pull; must bundle more volume, commit for several years, or credibly show the alternates
They have EPF payment delays and pending legal case(s) — watch for any supply hiccups
Their distress score (Altman Z 1.45) puts them in the grey zone — healthy today but closer to the edge than peers; don't squeeze so hard you tip a fragile supplier
We have no internal price benchmark (no bestPriceWePay) — rely on the market ask and the two strong alternates to anchor the target
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in a three-year commitment at ₹0.70 per cap and move to 15-day payment — that frees up cash for both of us and lets us grow the business together.
